statement: Zero is a natural number
For every natural number n, S(n) is a natural number (closure under successor)
formal_expression: forall n in N: S(n) in N

statement: For every natural number n, S(n) is not equal to zero
For all natural numbers m and n, if S(m) = S(n) then m = n (injectivity of successor)
formal_expression: forall m,n in N: S(m) = S(n) -> m = n

statement: If a property holds for zero and for the successor of every natural number for which it holds, then it holds for all natural numbers (induction)
formal_expression: (P(0) and forall n: P(n) -> P(S(n))) -> forall n: P(n)

statement: A proposition cannot be both true and false at the same time (law of non-contradiction)
Every proposition is either true or false (law of excluded middle)
A proposition is equivalent to its double negation (law of double negation elimination)
If P implies Q and P is true, then Q is true (modus ponens)
If P implies Q and Q is false, then P is false (modus tollens)
formal_expression: (P -> Q) and not Q |- not P

statement: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another (conservation of energy)
The total momentum of an isolated system remains constant (conservation of momentum)
The speed of light in vacuum is constant for all inertial observers
The laws of physics are the same in all inertial reference frames (principle of relativity)
The entropy of an isolated system never decreases (second law of thermodynamics)
Theological claims operate within frameworks of faith that are logically structured but axiomatically distinct from empirical science
The problem of evil is a valid logical structure: the co-existence of omnipotence, omniscience, omnibenevolence, and evil requires reconciliation
Theological diversity is an empirical fact: multiple internally consistent theological frameworks exist with non-overlapping axiom sets
The ontological argument has a valid logical form: whether its premises are true is a separate question from whether the inference is valid
Apophatic theology (knowledge by negation) is a coherent epistemic approach: stating what the divine is not can be logically rigorous
Cogito ergo sum: the act of thinking presupposes the existence of the thinker
Knowledge requires at minimum justified true belief (the classical tripartite analysis), though sufficiency is debated
The map is not the territory: all models are representations, not the things they represent
The problem of induction: no finite number of observations can logically guarantee a universal conclusion
Hume's guillotine: normative statements (ought) cannot be derived solely from descriptive statements (is)
All matter is composed of atoms, which are the smallest units of a chemical element retaining that element's properties
In any chemical reaction, mass is conserved: the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products (law of conservation of mass)
Elements combine in fixed, definite proportions by mass to form compounds (law of definite proportions)
The periodic table organizes elements by atomic number, and elements in the same group share similar chemical properties
Chemical bonds form because the resulting arrangement of electrons and nuclei has lower total energy than the separate atoms
All living organisms are composed of one or more cells, and the cell is the basic unit of life
All cells arise from pre-existing cells through cell division
DNA is the hereditary material in all known cellular organisms, encoding the instructions for building and maintaining the organism
Natural selection acts on heritable variation in fitness, producing adaptation over generations
Homeostasis: living systems maintain internal stability through self-regulating feedback mechanisms
A Turing machine can simulate any computation that any other physically realizable machine can perform (Church-Turing thesis)
The halting problem is undecidable: no algorithm can determine for every program-input pair whether the program eventually halts
Every deterministic algorithm has a well-defined worst-case time complexity expressible in Big-O notation
Boolean algebra with AND, OR, and NOT operations is functionally complete: any Boolean function can be expressed using these operators
Cryptographic hash functions map arbitrary data to fixed-size outputs such that finding collisions is computationally infeasible
Resources are scarce: human wants exceed available means, requiring allocation decisions
Rational agents respond to incentives: changing costs or benefits of an action changes the likelihood of that action
Voluntary trade creates value: both parties to a voluntary exchange expect to be better off, or they would not trade
Opportunity cost: the true cost of any choice is the value of the best alternative forgone
In a Nash equilibrium, no player can improve their payoff by unilaterally changing their strategy
formal_expression: forall i: u_i(s_i*, s_{-i}*) >= u_i(s_i, s_{-i}*)

statement: All human languages have recursive syntactic structure: sentences can contain embedded sentences
The relationship between a linguistic sign (word) and its referent is arbitrary (Saussure's principle of arbitrariness)
Every natural language can express any concept expressible in any other natural language, given sufficient elaboration (expressibility hypothesis)
All known human languages distinguish between nouns and verbs at the functional level
Formal grammars can be classified by the Chomsky hierarchy into four nested classes of increasing generative power
Human working memory has a limited capacity, approximately 7 plus or minus 2 items (Miller's law)
Behavior is jointly determined by the organism and its environment; neither alone is sufficient explanation
Cognitive dissonance: holding contradictory beliefs simultaneously creates psychological tension that motivates belief revision
Reinforcement increases the probability of a behavior; punishment decreases it (law of effect)
Perception is an active constructive process: the brain interprets sensory input using prior knowledge and expectations
Social facts are emergent: collective phenomena (norms, institutions) cannot be reduced entirely to individual psychology
Network effects: the value of a network to each participant grows with the number of participants
Social stratification is a universal feature of human societies: all known societies exhibit inequality in resource distribution
The tragedy of the commons: individually rational exploitation of shared resources leads to collective depletion without governance mechanisms
Institutions reduce transaction costs by establishing shared rules, norms, and enforcement mechanisms
The universe is expanding: the distance between galaxies is increasing over time, as observed through cosmological redshift
The cosmological principle: on sufficiently large scales, the universe is homogeneous and isotropic
The cosmic microwave background radiation is thermal blackbody radiation at approximately 2.725 Kelvin, permeating the entire observable universe
The observable universe has a finite age, estimated at approximately 13.8 billion years from the initial singularity
The gravitational constant G is a fundamental physical constant relating mass to gravitational force
The entropy of a discrete random variable quantifies the average information content per observation (Shannon entropy)
No lossless compression algorithm can compress all possible inputs; any algorithm that shortens some inputs must lengthen others (pigeonhole principle)
The channel capacity theorem: reliable communication is possible at any rate below channel capacity, and impossible above it (Shannon's noisy channel coding theorem)
Mutual information is non-negative: observing one variable can never decrease knowledge about another on average
Landauer's principle: erasing one bit of information requires a minimum energy dissipation of kT*ln(2)
Ethical claims are categorically distinct from empirical claims: 'ought' statements require normative justification beyond factual description
The universalizability principle: a moral rule is valid only if it could be consistently applied to all agents in similar circumstances
Moral dilemmas exist: situations arise where valid ethical principles conflict, and no resolution satisfies all principles simultaneously
The principle of moral consideration: any entity capable of having interests has some claim to moral consideration
Consequentialism, deontology, and virtue ethics are three irreducible families of ethical reasoning, each capturing genuine moral intuitions
